nodes.label: Phonons

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D060739

nodes.label: Density functional theory

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000077318

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Density functional theory as: A theory that is used to describe the electronic ground state properties of matter. It forms the basis of methods in obtaining a solution to the Schrodinger equation for a many-body system, and to investigate the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of molecules and materials.

nodes.label: Higgs mechanism

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

nodes.summary: CERN describes the Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism as the interaction by which elementary particles gain mass through the Higgs field. It states that stronger interaction gives greater mass, while photons do not interact with the field and have no mass.

nodes.label: Higgs boson

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/higgs-boson/

nodes.summary: CERN describes the Higgs boson as a wave in the Higgs field. It reports that the particle announced by ATLAS and CMS on 4 July 2012 was concluded, after additional data in March 2013, to be some kind of Higgs boson.

nodes.label: Quarks

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

nodes.summary: CERN describes quarks as one of two basic types of matter particles, with six members arranged in three generations: up and down, charm and strange, top and bottom. It states that quarks have three colour types and combine into colourless objects.

nodes.label: Leptons

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

nodes.summary: CERN describes six leptons arranged in three generations: electron and electron neutrino, muon and muon neutrino, tau and tau neutrino. The charged electron, muon and tau are distinguished from electrically neutral neutrinos with very small mass.

nodes.label: Gluons

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://home.cern/science/physics/standard-model/

nodes.summary: CERN identifies gluons as boson force carriers responsible for the strong force in the Standard Model.

nodes.label: Nuclear physics

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009686

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nuclear physics as: The study of the characteristics, behavior, and internal structures of the atomic nucleus and its interactions with other nuclei. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

nodes.label: Nuclear fission

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009680

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nuclear fission as: Nuclear reaction in which the nucleus of a heavy atom such as uranium or plutonium is split into two approximately equal parts by a neutron, charged particle, or photon.

nodes.label: Nuclear fusion

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009681

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nuclear fusion as: Thermonuclear reaction in which the nuclei of an element of low atomic weight unite under extremely high temperature and pressure to form a nucleus of a heavier atom.

nodes.label: Stellar evolution

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

nodes.summary: NASA describes a star's life cycle as formation from collapsing clouds of gas and dust, a long phase powered by hydrogen fusion, and later changes whose outcomes depend strongly on stellar mass.

nodes.label: White dwarfs

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

nodes.summary: In its account of low-mass stellar death, NASA describes a white dwarf as the remaining stellar core after the outer layers are expelled, a roughly Earth-sized remnant that cools over billions of years.

nodes.label: Neutron stars

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

nodes.summary: NASA identifies a neutron star as one possible extremely dense surviving core remnant of a high-mass star after a core-collapse supernova.

nodes.label: Supernovae

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/

nodes.summary: NASA describes a core-collapse supernova of a high-mass star as a huge explosion driven by the collapse and rebound of an iron core, sending a shock wave outward and leaving a dense remnant such as a neutron star or black hole.

nodes.label: Accretion disks

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/black-holes/

nodes.summary: NASA describes accretion disks around black holes as rings of gas and dust that emit light across many wavelengths, including X-rays.

nodes.label: Cosmic microwave background

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

nodes.summary: NASA describes the cosmic microwave background as early-universe light decoupled from matter about 380,000 years after the Big Bang and stretched by cosmic expansion to a glow at about 2.7 kelvin.

nodes.label: Inflationary cosmology

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

nodes.summary: NASA describes the inflation hypothesis as a brief period of extraordinary expansion connected to the formation of large-scale cosmic structure. It identifies CMB observations as a probe and states that the physical process behind inflation remains unknown.

nodes.label: Big Bang nucleosynthesis

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/overview/

nodes.summary: In its account of cosmic history, NASA describes Big Bang nucleosynthesis as the early period when collisions of protons and neutrons produced hydrogen, helium and traces of lithium and beryllium, before expansion and cooling stopped further element formation.

nodes.label: Large-scale structure

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://science.nasa.gov/astrophysics/programs/physics-of-the-cosmos/big-bang-and-the-evolution-of-the-universe/

nodes.summary: NASA describes galaxies and galaxy clusters as the large-scale structure associated, in its inflation account, with the growth of small early density fluctuations.

nodes.summary: Source-attributed description: The cited LZ and ADMX analyses test different proposed dark-matter signals: WIMP-induced xenon nuclear recoils and axion signals in a strong-field microwave cavity, respectively. Their exclusions apply under their separate stated assumptions.

nodes.summary: Source-attributed description: Six very short events discussed as PBH or free-floating-planet candidates.

nodes.label: SH0ES baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result
nodes.summary: The SH0ES analysis reports a baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result of 73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, including systematics.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Measurement of the Local Value of the Hubble Constant with 1 km/s/Mpc Uncertainty from the Hubble Space Telescope and the SH0ES Team

nodes.label: A Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity
nodes.summary: Bose and coauthors reported a proposal for a laboratory test in which gravitational interaction between two micron-size test masses could entangle them, with correlations between one embedded spin in each test mass proposed as the entanglement witness.

sources.title: A Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity

nodes.label: LZ 4.2 tonne-year WIMP search background consistency
nodes.summary: In the LUX-ZEPLIN 4.2 tonne-year WIMP dark-matter search, the collaboration reported no evidence for an excess over expected backgrounds after removing artificial signal-like events injected to mitigate analyzer bias.

sources.title: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

nodes.label: LZ 4.2 tonne-year WIMP search reported no excess
nodes.summary: In its 4.2 tonne-year WIMP dark-matter search, LUX-ZEPLIN reported no evidence for an excess over expected backgrounds after removal of artificial signal-like events injected to mitigate analyzer bias.

sources.title: Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

nodes.label: Bose et al. gravitational entanglement test proposal
nodes.summary: Bose and collaborators proposed a test in which gravitationally induced phase evolution between two micron-size test masses in adjacent matter-wave interferometers could produce detectable entanglement, with the masses separated sufficiently to keep Casimir-Polder forces at bay.

sources.title: A Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity

nodes.label: DESI DR2 flat-LambdaCDM fit with mild BAO-CMB tension
nodes.summary: DESI reported that its DR2 BAO results were well described by a flat LambdaCDM model while the parameters preferred by BAO were in mild 2.3-sigma tension with those determined from the CMB.

sources.title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints

nodes.label: DES Y6 reported weak preference for evolving dark energy
nodes.summary: The DES Collaboration reported that its analyzed probe combinations supported a weak preference for evolving dark energy, with the significance of deviation from a cosmological constant ranging from 2.3 to 3.2 sigma when individual probes were left out.

sources.title: Constraints on Dynamical Dark Energy from Multiple Probes in the Full Dark Energy Survey

nodes.label: DESI DR2 BAO consistency with DR1, SDSS and supernova distances
nodes.summary: The retained DESI DR2 source reports that its BAO results are consistent with DESI DR1 and SDSS, and that their distance-redshift relationship matches recent supernova compilations over the same redshift range.

sources.title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints

nodes.label: WHO sixth-edition semen examination and processing procedures
nodes.summary: The WHO sixth-edition semen manual describes procedures and methods for laboratory examination and processing of human semen.

sources.title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th ed

nodes.label: WHO-described clinical and research uses of semen analysis
nodes.summary: The WHO semen manual states that semen analysis may be useful for investigating male fertility status and monitoring spermatogenesis during and following male fertility regulation and other interventions, in clinical and research settings.

sources.title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th ed

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM varicocelectomy recommendation for selected infertile men
nodes.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends considering surgical varicocelectomy for men attempting conception who have palpable varicoceles, infertility and abnormal semen parameters, except azoospermic men; it labels this a moderate recommendation supported by Grade B evidence.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM microdissection sperm retrieval recommendation in NOA
nodes.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends microdissection testicular sperm extraction for men with non-obstructive azoospermia undergoing sperm retrieval, assigning a moderate recommendation with Grade C evidence.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM recommendation against testosterone monotherapy when fertility is desired
nodes.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline states that testosterone monotherapy should not be prescribed to a male interested in current or future fertility, identifying this recommendation as a clinical principle.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM uncertainty regarding fertility supplements
nodes.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline reports that clear, reliable evidence is lacking for supplements offered to men attempting conception and describes their value for improving fertility outcomes as questionable.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM sperm banking recommendation before gonadotoxic therapy
nodes.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline advises clinicians to encourage sperm banking, preferably multiple specimens when possible, before gonadotoxic therapy or other cancer treatment that may affect male fertility; it classifies this as expert opinion.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: AUA/ASRM-reported gaps in understanding male infertility causes
nodes.summary: In its future-directions discussion, the AUA/ASRM guideline states that the causes of male infertility, including their genetic basis, had been only superficially explained at the time of the guideline.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

nodes.label: Endocrine Society hypogonadism diagnostic criteria
nodes.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends diagnosing hypogonadism only in men with compatible symptoms and signs and unequivocally and consistently low serum testosterone concentrations.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

nodes.label: Endocrine Society recommendation for repeat morning testosterone measurement
nodes.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends confirming hypogonadism by repeating measurement of morning fasting total testosterone concentrations.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

nodes.label: Endocrine Society hormonal evaluation of primary versus secondary hypogonadism
nodes.summary: For men with hypogonadism, the Endocrine Society guideline recommends measuring serum luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone concentrations to distinguish primary testicular from secondary pituitary-hypothalamic hypogonadism.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

nodes.label: Endocrine Society recommendation against routine population screening for hypogonadism
nodes.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends against routine screening of men in the general population for hypogonadism.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

nodes.label: Inferred Dresser geyserite at three localities
nodes.summary: Djokic and colleagues interpret microlaminated siliceous rocks at three Dresser Formation DFc1 localities, approximately 2 km apart, as geyserite.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Dresser siliceous ridges interpreted as sinter terracettes
nodes.summary: At Dresser locality 1S, the authors interpret convex siliceous ridges above stratiform geyserite as resembling mid- to distal-apron hot-spring sinter terracettes.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Dresser barite masses interpreted as fossil hot-spring pools
nodes.summary: The authors propose that at least some large Dresser barite masses at hydrothermal vein tips are mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot-spring pools and shallow hydrothermal plumbing.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Inferred gas-bubble preservation in Dresser microbial EPS
nodes.summary: The authors interpret roughly 200 µm circular structures in Dresser geyserite as gas bubbles likely trapped in microbial EPS, while leaving thermal-fluid versus metabolic gas origin unresolved.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Dresser quartz fabric proposed as microbial palisade texture
nodes.summary: The authors suggest that bedding-normal quartz crystals in Dresser sinter terracettes are analogous to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric formed by silicified filaments.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Dresser stromatolitic laminates associated with sinter clasts
nodes.summary: At Dresser locality 24S, geyserite rip-up clasts occur among domical and conical stromatolitic laminates; their internal laminae and sediment onlap are described as consistent with microbial origin.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

nodes.label: Dresser microfossil-like vesicles interpreted as volcanic glass
nodes.summary: A 2018 study interprets spheroidal-to-lenticular Dresser microstructures resembling Archean microfossils as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass based on size, wall ultrastructure and chemistry.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

nodes.label: Kerogenous carbon associated with Dresser volcanic vesicles
nodes.summary: In the studied Dresser volcanic-glass microstructures, organic kerogenous material accompanies altered glass, with some vesicles lined or filled by carbon and organic-rich laminae enveloping multiple vesicles.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

nodes.label: Isolated volcanic vesicles can imitate microfossils
nodes.summary: The Dresser pseudo-fossil study cautions that isolated reworked silicified volcanic vesicles can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, complicating early-life identification; nanoscale wall analysis may be required to exclude biogenicity.

sources.title: Volcanogenic Pseudo-Fossils from the ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation, Pilbara, Western Australia

nodes.label: Nutrient limitation conditions basalt microbial element release
nodes.summary: In laboratory incubations of HSDP2 drill-core basalt with Burkholderia fungorum, release of Fe and other major elements exceeded abiotic controls only for nutrient-depleted rock-sample assays.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

nodes.label: Synthetic basalt glass stress and Fe(II) track element release
nodes.summary: In biotic laboratory colonization assays using synthetic basaltic glasses, dissolved major-element concentrations increased with greater residual stress and Fe(II) content.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

nodes.label: Biofilm coverage differs across synthetic basalt glass types
nodes.summary: The 2018 colonization assays reported dense biofilm on stressed Fe(II)-rich basalt glasses, versus sparse colonization on unstressed Fe(III)-rich glasses.

sources.title: Experimental Microbial Alteration and Fe Mobilization From Basaltic Rocks of the ICDP HSDP2 Drill Core, Hilo, Hawaii

nodes.label: CDLI P000005 Uruk IV lexical tablet metadata
nodes.summary: CDLI catalogs P000005 (museum number VAT 15153) as a clay lexical tablet from Uruk (modern Warka), assigned to Uruk IV (ca. 3350–3200 BC), held in the Vorderasiatisches Museum, Berlin, with language undetermined.

sources.title: CDLI Lexical 000002, ex. 172 (P000005)

nodes.label: CDLI P000005 column-one lexical signs and witness classification
nodes.summary: CDLI transcribes P000005 obverse column 1 as 1(N01) with ESZDA#, KAB, and DI@t?, marks the remainder broken, and lists the tablet as a witness to the Archaic Lu2 A composite P464118.

sources.title: CDLI Lexical 000002, ex. 172 (P000005)

nodes.label: Distinct Ur III and Old Babylonian literary catalogue entries in ETCSL
nodes.summary: ETCSL separately lists an Ur III catalogue from Nibru (N1), an Old Babylonian catalogue from Nibru (N2), and an Old Babylonian catalogue possibly from Zimbir (B1); these listings do not themselves establish a transmission path among the catalogues.

sources.title: The Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature: Catalogue of all available compositions and translations

nodes.label: ETCSL listings for Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa Versions A and B
nodes.summary: ETCSL catalogs Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa as separate Version A (1.8.1.5) and Version B (1.8.1.5.1) entries, each offering transliteration and translation; those entries alone establish no copying direction or relative date.

sources.title: The Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature: Catalogue of all available compositions and translations

nodes.label: SAA 01 001 royal letter cataloguing and date limits
nodes.summary: SAAo catalogs SAA 01 001 (CDLI P224485; primary publication NL 039) as a Neo-Assyrian clay administrative letter from the Northwest Palace archive at Nimrud, attributed to Sargon II’s reign (721–705 BC) but explicitly undated, with sender the king and addressee Aššur-šarru-u[ṣur].

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

nodes.label: Reported Midas messenger and alliance claim in SAA 01 001
nodes.summary: In SAA 01 001 the royal writer quotes an earlier report that a messenger [of] Midas brought 14 men of Que previously sent by Urik to Urarṭu and declares that the Phrygian became an ally; these are reported statements in the letter, not independent verification of either event.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

nodes.label: SAA 01 001 instruction to maintain Phrygian messenger contact
nodes.summary: SAA 01 001 directs its recipient not to withdraw a messenger from the Phrygian, to write amicably, and to monitor news about him; the instruction does not establish that the recipient complied.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

nodes.label: Threatened two-sided pressure against Tabal in SAA 01 001
nodes.summary: In SAA 01 001 the royal writer proposes that the recipient pressure the kings of Tabal from one side while the Phrygian does so from the other; the source includes an ellipsis and does not confirm that the plan occurred.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

nodes.label: Sennacherib 015 claims confinement of Hezekiah in Jerusalem
nodes.summary: In RINAP Sennacherib 015, the first-person royal narrator claims to have confined Hezekiah in Jerusalem like a bird in a cage; this records an inscriptional claim rather than independent proof of the campaign outcome.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015

nodes.label: Sennacherib 015 claims diversion of the Tebilti River
nodes.summary: In column vi of RINAP Sennacherib 015, the royal narrator reports changing the Tebilti River’s course, repairing erosion damage, and directing its outflow, with several portions of the translation editorially restored.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015

nodes.label: Sennacherib 015 reports Nineveh orchard plots and a canal route
nodes.summary: In column viii of RINAP Sennacherib 015, the royal narrator reports dividing upstream meadowland into plots of two pānu for Nineveh’s citizens and cutting a canal from near Kisiri toward Nineveh’s plain; parts of the canal construction and route appear in brackets as editorial restorations.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015

nodes.label: Three presentations of universal properties in Leinster’s textbook
nodes.summary: Leinster describes his introductory category theory textbook as presenting universal properties through adjoint functors, representable functors, and limits, with a final chapter tying the three approaches together.

sources.title: Basic Category Theory

nodes.label: Seven-sketch application tour of category theory
nodes.summary: Fong and Spivak describe seven instructional sketches pairing examples including databases, electric circuits, and dynamical systems with categorical structures including adjoint functors, enriched categories, and toposes.

sources.title: Seven Sketches in Compositionality: An Invitation to Applied Category Theory

nodes.label: Database schemas as categories and instances as functors
nodes.summary: Spivak proposes a database definition language in which a database schema is a small category and an instance is a set-valued functor on that schema.

sources.title: Functorial Data Migration

nodes.label: Three schema-induced data-migration functors
nodes.summary: Within Spivak’s category-and-functor database model, morphisms of schemas induce three data-migration functors that translate instances between schemas in canonical ways.

sources.title: Functorial Data Migration

nodes.label: Data-migration functors parameterize relational operations
nodes.summary: Spivak reports that the three data-migration functors parameterize projections, unions, and joins across all tables simultaneously in the categorical database formulation.

sources.title: Functorial Data Migration

nodes.label: Categorical migration functors as alternatives to query types
nodes.summary: Spivak states that his three data-migration functors can be used in place of conjunctive and disjunctive queries within the paper’s database framework.

sources.title: Functorial Data Migration

nodes.label: Functorial connection to functional-programming types
nodes.summary: Spivak describes connecting a database to a functional programming language by introducing a functorial connection between the database schema and the language’s category of types.

sources.title: Functorial Data Migration

nodes.label: Higher Gray tensor generalization described as open
nodes.summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber describe the systematic construction of higher-dimensional analogues of the Gray tensor product as an open problem in higher category theory in their 2009-submitted paper.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

nodes.label: Gray and Crans tensor products included in higher-operad theory
nodes.summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber state that their resulting theory includes the Gray tensor product of 2-categories and the Crans tensor product of Gray categories.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

nodes.label: Reported Ekmann-Hilton result for braided monoidal 2-categories
nodes.summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber report obtaining an “Ekmann-Hilton” result for braided monoidal 2-categories as an application of their higher-operad framework.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

nodes.label: Tensor product construction for A-infinity algebras
nodes.summary: Batanin, Cisinski, and Weber state that their paper gives a construction of a tensor product of A-infinity algebras.

sources.title: Algebras of higher operads as enriched categories II

nodes.label: NIST controlled blocking
nodes.summary: NIST describes blocking as holding nuisance factors constant inside homogeneous blocks while varying the factor of interest.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods: 5.3.3.2. Randomized block designs

nodes.label: NIST balanced blocking criterion
nodes.summary: NIST defines a blocking factor by equal occurrence of each primary-factor level at each nuisance-factor level.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods: 5.3.3.2. Randomized block designs

nodes.label: NIST residual nuisance randomization
nodes.summary: NIST recommends blocking important nuisance variables and randomizing to reduce contamination by remaining nuisance variables.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods: 5.3.3.2. Randomized block designs

nodes.label: NIST hypothetical blocked wafer allocation
nodes.summary: NIST illustrates a hypothetical design putting four wafers with different dosages in each of three furnace runs.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods: 5.3.3.2. Randomized block designs

nodes.label: Nosek preregistration definition
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. (2018) define analysis preregistration as committing to analytic steps without prior knowledge of outcomes.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek postdiction diagnosticity warning
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. warn that postdictive NHST analyses may yield p-values of unknown diagnosticity.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek 2018 preregistration evidence limit
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. (2018) report theoretical and correlational support for preregistration but insufficient experimental evidence of a reproducibility advantage.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek preexisting-data blinding
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. explain that tests of predictions using preexisting data depend on blinded analysis decisions, which face risks when data have already been observed.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek biased preregistered decision trees
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. warn that preregistered decision trees can still embed bias, such as stopping after achieving p < 0.05.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek complete reporting across studies
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. argue that reporting all planned outcomes matters because preregistration alone cannot eliminate multiple-comparison and selective-reporting problems.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek Registered Reports workflow
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. describe Registered Reports as pre-outcome methodological peer review with in-principle acceptance, followed by review of execution and adherence.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Nosek exploratory-to-holdout testing
nodes.summary: Nosek et al. describe splitting a dataset, sealing the holdout and preregistering exploration-derived predictions before unsealing it.

sources.title: The preregistration revolution

nodes.label: Ptolemy's four seasonal lunar-syzygy markers
nodes.summary: In Tetrabiblos II.10, Ptolemy proposes using new- and full-moon syzygies preceding the four equinoctial and solstitial starting points to conjecture seasonal conditions for spring, summer, autumn and winter.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

nodes.label: Ptolemy's daily fixed-star weather intensifications
nodes.summary: In Tetrabiblos II.12, Ptolemy attributes day-by-day intensification of weather qualities chiefly to appearances of bright fixed stars at their morning or evening rising or setting relative to the Sun.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

nodes.label: Ptolemy's lunar halo weather signs
nodes.summary: In Tetrabiblos II.13, Ptolemy treats a single clear fading lunar halo as a fair-weather sign and multiple or differently colored and shaped lunar halos as signs of storms or winds.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, Book II, Sections 10–13: Seasonal and Detailed Weather Predictions

nodes.label: Aratus's early-crescent weather signs
nodes.summary: In Phaenomena, Aratus presents the shape and color of the Moon's horns on the third and fourth nights as signs for calm, wind, rain and storms, including directional winds linked to horn orientation.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

nodes.label: Aratus's Manger and Asses wind-rain signs
nodes.summary: Aratus states that a darkening or vanishing Manger in Cancer signals rain or storms, and that relative dimming of the northern or southern Ass star can indicate a southerly or northerly wind.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

nodes.label: Aratus's seabird and shorebird wind signs
nodes.summary: Aratus describes a heron flying landward from the sea with cries, storm petrels turning toward winds, and ducks or gulls beating wings on shore as signs preceding gales.

sources.title: Aratus, Phaenomena: Zodiac Risings and Weather Signs

nodes.label: Theophrastus's local mountain-cloud weather guidance
nodes.summary: Theophrastus says mountainous and coastal terrain affects cloud movements when winds change and advises attending to local conditions and knowledgeable local observers when interpreting weather signs.

sources.title: Theophrastus, Concerning Weather Signs (De Signis)

nodes.label: Theophrastus's red-sky rain time window
nodes.summary: Theophrastus describes a reddish sky before sunrise as a rain sign for the same day or within three days, and a red sunset sky as a similar but less certain sign.

sources.title: Theophrastus, Concerning Weather Signs (De Signis)

nodes.label: Theophrastus's ant-egg movement omens
nodes.summary: Theophrastus treats ants moving their eggs from hollow anthills to higher ground as a sign of rain and moving them down as a sign of fair weather.

sources.title: Theophrastus, Concerning Weather Signs (De Signis)

nodes.label: LTEE Cit+ emergence and Cit++ expansion
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) describe emergence of citrate utilization in the Ara−3 LTEE population after 31,500 generations and descendants fully exploiting citrate by 33,000 generations.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: CitT duplication fitness in early LTEE Cit+ isolate
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 2.2% competitive fitness advantage associated with the citT-activating duplication by comparing early Cit+ isolate ZDB564 with its Cit− revertant ZDB706.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Weak ancestral fitness benefit of aerobic citT activation
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 1.0% fitness advantage for the engineered Cit+ activation in ancestral LTEE strain REL606, with weak statistical support (one-tailed P = 0.033; n = 12).

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Deleterious citT activation in evolved genetic backgrounds
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) reported that activating citT reduced competitive fitness in 11 of 23 tested evolved pre-Cit+ clones, including five with reductions greater than 20%.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Negative Cit+ activation effect in intermediate Ara−3 phylogeny
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) estimated a −5.4% fitness effect (interval −7.2% to −3.6%) for citT activation in the intermediate pre-Cit+ lineage group represented by ZDB425, ZDB458 and ZDB464.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Late positive Cit+ activation effect in Ara−3 phylogeny
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) estimated a +2.4% fitness effect (95% interval +1.4% to +3.4%) in a later fully potentiated pre-Cit+ lineage group containing ZDB19 and ZDB13 from as early as 29,000 generations.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Ecological potentiation test in evolved generation-31,000 Ara−3 population mixture
nodes.summary: Leon et al. (2018) measured a 0.9% Cit+ fitness advantage when competing engineered ZDB706 variants at low frequency within the generation-31,000 LTEE population and reported no support for an ecological-potentiation advantage.

sources.title: Innovation in an E. coli evolution experiment is contingent on maintaining adaptive potential until competition subsides

nodes.label: Loss of detectable Cit− lineage in Ara−3 samples
nodes.summary: Turner et al. (2015) detected the Ara−3 Cit− genotype and phenotype through 43,500 LTEE generations but not in samples from 44,000 generations onward.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

nodes.label: Cit− persisted through 40 reconstructed evolution replays
nodes.summary: Turner et al. (2015) found Cit− persistence in all 20 replay populations from generation 43,500 and all 20 from generation 40,000 after 500 generations, plus one generation-43,000 replay propagated for 2,500 generations.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

nodes.label: Reinvasion of a 50,000-generation Cit+ population
nodes.summary: Turner et al. (2015) observed that a generation-43,000 Cit− clone reinvaded the generation-50,000 Ara−3 population, reaching about 3 × 10^5 cells/mL, roughly an order of magnitude below final Cit− densities in the other treatments.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

nodes.label: Turner extinction cause unresolved; random-catastrophe proposal
nodes.summary: Turner et al. (2015) stated that the Ara−3 Cit− lineage extinction cause remained unknown, rejected their initial ongoing Cit+ adaptation explanation, and proposed an unidentified rare perturbation as a possible cause rather than an observed event.

sources.title: Replaying Evolution to Test the Cause of Extinction of One Ecotype in an Experimentally Evolved Population

nodes.label: Liu et al. reported position-dependent retrieval in long inputs
nodes.summary: Liu and colleagues report that models evaluated on multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval often performed best when relevant information occurred at the start or end of a long input, with marked degradation for middle positions.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

nodes.label: RULER expands needle retrieval to multi-hop and aggregation
nodes.summary: The RULER paper describes a configurable synthetic long-context benchmark extending needle-in-a-haystack retrieval with different needle types and counts, plus multi-hop tracing and aggregation; it evaluates 17 language models on 13 representative tasks.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

nodes.label: RULER performance gap at claimed 32K context
nodes.summary: In the RULER authors’ evaluation of 17 long-context models advertised for at least 32K tokens, almost all declined on RULER as input length grew, and the authors reported only about half maintained satisfactory performance at 32K, despite nearly perfect results on vanilla needle retrieval.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?

nodes.label: NoLiMa tests retrieval without literal matching
nodes.summary: The NoLiMa authors introduce a needle-retrieval benchmark in which questions and relevant text have minimal lexical overlap, requiring latent associations rather than straightforward literal matching to locate evidence.

sources.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching

nodes.label: NoLiMa reported degradation in 13-model evaluation at 32K
nodes.summary: In NoLiMa evaluations of 13 models claiming at least 128K-token support, 11 performed at under half their short-context baseline at 32K; the reported GPT-4o score dropped from 99.3% at short context to 69.7% at 32K.

sources.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching

nodes.label: LongBench v2 realistic long-context question collection
nodes.summary: The LongBench v2 authors describe 503 multiple-choice questions with source contexts from 8,000 to 2 million words spanning six categories, including multi-document questions and code-repository understanding.

sources.title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks

nodes.label: LongBench v2 reported expert and model benchmark accuracies
nodes.summary: The LongBench v2 authors report 53.7% human-expert accuracy with a 15-minute limit, 50.1% for the strongest directly answering model, and 57.7% for o1-preview using longer reasoning under their reported evaluation.

sources.title: LongBench v2: Towards Deeper Understanding and Reasoning on Realistic Long-context Multitasks

nodes.label: BABILong distributes reasoning facts through long documents
nodes.summary: BABILong introduces 20 tasks involving fact chaining, induction, deduction, counting and lists or sets, designed to require reasoning over facts distributed through very long natural-language documents.

sources.title: BABILong: Testing the Limits of LLMs with Long Context Reasoning-in-a-Haystack

nodes.label: HELMET reported poor predictive validity of simple needle tests
nodes.summary: In a study of 59 long-context models, the HELMET authors report that synthetic needle-in-a-haystack scores do not reliably predict downstream performance and that their different application-centered task categories have low correlations.

sources.title: HELMET: How to Evaluate Long-Context Language Models Effectively and Thoroughly

nodes.label: InfinityBench longer-than-100K-token benchmark design
nodes.summary: The 2024 InfinityBench paper describes a benchmark with average data length above 100K tokens and a mix of synthetic and realistic English and Chinese tasks intended to require long-distance dependencies rather than retrieval of isolated passages.

sources.title: ∞Bench: Extending Long Context Evaluation Beyond 100K Tokens

nodes.label: Original LongBench multilingual multitask composition
nodes.summary: The original LongBench authors report 21 datasets in six task categories in English and Chinese, with average input lengths of 6,711 English words and 13,386 Chinese characters.

sources.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding

nodes.label: LongCite sentence-level citation generation workflow
nodes.summary: The LongCite authors propose a Coarse-to-Fine pipeline producing long-context question-answer pairs with sentence-level citations and report using its LongCite-45k training data to train LongCite-8B and LongCite-9B.

sources.title: LongCite: Enabling LLMs to Generate Fine-grained Citations in Long-context QA

nodes.label: JUNO 207-day atmospheric mass-splitting fits
nodes.summary: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported 8,294 inverse-beta-decay candidates in 207.2 live days at an average 52.5 km reactor baseline and obtained different fitted atmospheric mass splittings under normal and inverted ordering using a Daya Bay constraint.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

nodes.label: JUNO solar oscillation-parameter estimates
nodes.summary: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported sin²θ12=0.3036±0.0064 and Δm21²=(7.388±0.078)×10^-5 eV², with stated relative precisions of 2.1% and 1.1%, respectively.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

nodes.label: JUNO combined ordering indication and Bayes factor
nodes.summary: The September 2026 JUNO collaboration reported that incorporating long-baseline accelerator constraints on Δm31² favored normal over inverted neutrino mass ordering with one-sided significance of at least 2.1σ across CP-violating phases and a Bayesian Bayes factor of 10.18.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

nodes.label: KATRIN effective electron-antineutrino mass bound
nodes.summary: KATRIN reported a fitted squared effective electron-antineutrino mass of -0.14 (+0.13/-0.15) eV² from five tritium beta-decay campaigns and an effective-mass upper limit of 0.45 eV at 90% confidence using 259 measurement days and 36 million electrons.

sources.title: Direct neutrino-mass measurement based on 259 days of KATRIN data

nodes.label: KamLAND-Zen xenon-136 neutrinoless-decay half-life limit
nodes.summary: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset search with 745 kg enriched xenon and 2.1 tonne-years of xenon-136 exposure, combined with its previous phase, reported a 90%-confidence lower bound on the neutrinoless double-beta half-life of 3.8×10^26 years.

sources.title: Search for Majorana Neutrinos with the Complete KamLAND-Zen Dataset

nodes.label: KamLAND-Zen nuclear-model-dependent effective Majorana bound
nodes.summary: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset report translated its neutrinoless xenon-136 double-beta half-life constraint into effective Majorana neutrino-mass upper limits ranging from 28 to 122 meV using phenomenological nuclear matrix-element calculations.

sources.title: Search for Majorana Neutrinos with the Complete KamLAND-Zen Dataset

nodes.label: Planck 2018 plus BAO neutrino mass-sum bound
nodes.summary: The Planck 2018 cosmological-parameter analysis reported Σmν<0.12 eV as a 95% upper limit when combined with baryon acoustic oscillation data in its base spatially flat ΛCDM framework.

sources.title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters

nodes.label: DESI DR2 neutrino sum bound changes with dark-energy model
nodes.summary: The DESI DR2 analysis reported a 95% upper limit Σmν<0.064 eV for DESI BAO plus CMB under ΛCDM, versus Σmν<0.16 eV under a time-evolving w0wa dark-energy model using the same stated combination.

sources.title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints

nodes.label: DESI DR2 neutrino mass tension and boundary-sensitive inference
nodes.summary: The DESI DR2 neutrino-constraints analysis reported a Feldman-Cousins 95% bound Σmν<0.053 eV after correcting for the zero-mass boundary, below the oscillation-inferred lower limit, and a separate effective-mass parametrization yielding 3σ tension under its analysis assumptions.

sources.title: Constraints on Neutrino Physics from DESI DR2 BAO and DR1 Full Shape

nodes.label: Planck 2018 BAO mass bounds change under hierarchy priors
nodes.summary: A Bayesian reanalysis using Planck 2018 CMB plus BOSS DR12, MGS and 6dFGS BAO data reported 95%-confidence neutrino mass-sum limits of 0.12 eV (degenerate masses), 0.15 eV (normal ordering) and 0.17 eV (inverted ordering), attributing their differences to mass-sum priors.

sources.title: Updated results on neutrino mass and mass hierarchy from cosmology with Planck 2018 likelihoods

nodes.label: DESI and CMB neutrino constraints with isocurvature allowed
nodes.summary: A 2026 joint CMB, DESI DR2 and supernova analysis reported that allowing a neutrino-density isocurvature mode shifted its 95% neutrino mass-sum limits from 0.052 to 0.057 eV under ΛCDM and 0.111 to 0.115 eV under dynamical dark energy, without detecting the isocurvature mode.

sources.title: Constraints on the Sum of Neutrino Masses from ACT DR6 and DESI DR2 Considering Isocurvature Initial Conditions

nodes.label: Hierarchy-aware prior relaxes cosmological mass-sum bound
nodes.summary: The 2026 cosmological isocurvature analysis reported that its purely adiabatic ΛCDM upper limit of 0.052 eV lay below the oscillation-implied normal-ordering minimum of 0.05878 eV because of a statistical prior extending to zero, while a hierarchy-informed prior raised the reported upper limit to 0.092 eV.

sources.title: Constraints on the Sum of Neutrino Masses from ACT DR6 and DESI DR2 Considering Isocurvature Initial Conditions

nodes.label: Kurvers spatial producer-scrounger evolutionary simulation
nodes.summary: Kurvers and colleagues modeled group foraging with a spatially explicit genetic algorithm whose simulated agents could alternate between producing and scrounging; the exploration level and the probability of scrounging were distinct, evolving continuous traits each ranging from 0 to 1.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

nodes.label: Foraging patch density shifts exploration and scrounging in simulation
nodes.summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, increasing food-patch density favored higher exploration; it also reduced scrounging at low or intermediate patch richness, but this reduction disappeared at high patch richness.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

nodes.label: Food patch richness increases modeled scrounging
nodes.summary: In the Kurvers producer-scrounger simulations, richer food patches increased evolved scrounging propensities among both fast and slow explorers, while patch richness showed no effect on evolved exploration.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

nodes.label: No stable explorer-type polymorphism within simulated environments
nodes.summary: In the Kurvers evolutionary simulations, populations within a given environmental run approached one exploration optimum rather than retaining a stable coexistence of distinct explorer personality types.

sources.title: The Effect of Exploration on the Use of Producer-Scrounger Tactics

nodes.label: Thornton meerkat provisioning and monitoring sample sizes
nodes.summary: Thornton analyzed 1,070 scorpion feeds by 347 meerkat helpers to 339 pups from 137 litters in 15 groups for prey-provisioning state, and recorded monitoring times for 6,148 feeds by 300 helpers to 244 pups from 65 litters in 13 groups.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

nodes.label: Meerkat pup age predicts intact versus disabled scorpion feeds
nodes.summary: In Thornton’s wild meerkat scorpion-feeding analysis, older pups were less likely to receive dead or disabled scorpions and more likely to receive intact scorpions, adjusting for significant modeled covariates.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

nodes.label: Helper age versus previous pup-care experience in scorpion provisioning
nodes.summary: In Thornton’s meerkat scorpion-provisioning analysis, older eligible helpers were more likely to give pups intact scorpions, whereas prior experience with earlier foraging litters showed no statistically significant association after controlling for helper age.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

nodes.label: Meerkat pup monitoring varies with prey movement size and pup age
nodes.summary: For 6,148 observed meerkat pup feeds, helpers spent longer monitoring pups when provisioned prey was moving or larger and spent less time monitoring as pups grew older.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

nodes.label: Meerkat monitoring duration declines with nearby helpers and rain
nodes.summary: In Thornton’s meerkat feeding observations, pup monitoring duration decreased with larger litter size, higher recent rainfall, and the presence of another helper within two metres.

sources.title: Variation in contributions to teaching by meerkats

nodes.label: Ba-La-Cu-O: tentative 30 K onset (1986)
nodes.summary: Bednorz and Mueller reported an abrupt resistivity decrease of up to three orders of magnitude in multiphase, oxygen-deficient polycrystalline Ba-La-Cu-O samples, with the highest onset in the 30 K range and suppression at high current density; they described this as reminiscent of percolative superconductivity.

nodes.label: Mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O: 80–93 K transition (1987)
nodes.summary: NASA’s catalogue summary of Wu et al. reports a stable, reproducible superconductivity transition between 80 and 93 K in a mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O compound system at ambient pressure, maintained in a liquid-nitrogen Dewar.

nodes.label: YBCO grain-boundary orientation limits (1988)
nodes.summary: Dimos et al. measured grain-boundary critical current densities as a function of basal-plane misorientation in YBCO bicrystals and concluded that strong texture both normal to and within the basal plane is important for very high critical currents in pure polycrystalline samples.

nodes.label: Biaxially textured metal substrates for YBCO tapes (1996)
nodes.summary: Goyal et al. reported a route using industrially scalable thermomechanical texturing of flexible metal substrates followed by epitaxial buffer layers and YBa2Cu3Ox films; the deposited films carried critical currents at 77 K in zero field and had field dependencies similar to epitaxial films on single-crystal ceramic substrates.

nodes.label: YBCO tricrystal half-flux evidence (1994)
nodes.summary: Tsuei et al. used scanning SQUID microscopy at 4.2 K to observe spontaneous half-flux-quantum magnetization in a YBa2Cu3O7-delta ring with three grain-boundary Josephson junctions, but not in the two-junction rings; the authors reported consistency with d-wave pairing symmetry.

nodes.label: BaZrO3 additions enhance YBCO in-field current (2004)
nodes.summary: MacManus-Driscoll et al. reported that BaZrO3 additions to pulsed-laser-deposited YBCO films improved thickness-accounted in-field critical current densities by about 1.5–2 times over roughly 1–5 T and about 5 times at 7 T in the studied single-crystal and IBAD-MgO substrate samples; the transport study used 75.5 K and associated the enhancement with stronger vortex pinning.

nodes.label: Industrial YBCO/Y2O3 tape for high-field fusion magnets
nodes.summary: Molodyk et al. reported over 300 km of 4 mm-wide YBCO wire manufactured in nine months, with most delivered to CFS. In tested B-parallel-c samples with a 40 micrometre substrate and 5 micrometre copper stabilizer per side, engineering current density exceeded 1000 A/mm² at 20 K and 20 T and 2000 A/mm² at 4.2 K and 20 T; the formulation used Y2O3 nanoparticles without c-axis-correlated nanocolumnar defects.

nodes.label: SPARC TFMC: NINT stack-in-plate magnet
nodes.summary: Hartwig et al. described the built TFMC as a no-insulation, no-twist REBCO stack-in-plate magnet using 270 km of tape, weighing 10058 kg, with 16 single-pancake modules and two termination plates. REBCO stacks occupy spiral plate channels, with single-pass supercritical-helium coolant channels on the other side; vacuum-pressure solder impregnation provides mechanical protection and thermal/electrical connectivity.

nodes.label: SPARC TFMC: 20.1 T magnet demonstration
nodes.summary: Hartwig et al. reported TFMC reaching 20.1 T peak field on the conductor at 40.5 kA terminal current, with 815 kN/m Lorentz loading on the REBCO stacks and almost 1 GPa stress accommodated by the structural case.

nodes.label: SPARC TFMC: demountable nanohm joints
nodes.summary: Hartwig et al. reported fifteen internal demountable pancake-to-pancake TFMC joints operating with resistance in the 0.5–2.0 nanohm range at 20 K and magnetic fields up to 12 T.

nodes.label: SPARC TFMC: deliberate quench caused local damage
nodes.summary: Hartwig et al. reported localized thermal damage following an intentional open-circuit TFMC quench at 31.5 kA terminal current. The TFMC was deliberately not optimized for quench resiliency, so this experiment assessed passive self-protection rather than demonstrating damage-free protection for fusion-scale NINT coils.

nodes.label: High-field REBCO fusion pathway: proposal and qualification
nodes.summary: Hartwig et al. describe a proposed fusion pathway using REBCO superconducting toroidal-field coils above 20 T peak field on the coil, corresponding to 8–12 T in the plasma center. The model-coil program qualifies representative-scale magnet technology for this pathway; stand-alone magnet qualification is distinct from demonstrated fusion electricity generation.

nodes.label: ALCE evaluates fluency, correctness and citation quality
nodes.summary: Gao et al. (2023) report that ALCE uses automatic metrics for fluency, correctness, and citation quality and that these metrics correlate strongly with human judgments.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

nodes.label: ALCE ELI5 evaluation found incomplete citation support
nodes.summary: Gao et al. (2023) report that even the best models in their ELI5 evaluation lacked complete citation support 50% of the time.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

nodes.label: ContextCite contextual attribution method
nodes.summary: Cohen-Wang et al. (2024) introduce ContextCite as a scalable method for attributing generated statements to supplied context, designed to operate on top of existing language models.

sources.title: ContextCite: Attributing Model Generation to Context

nodes.label: Three-level evaluation of citation support
nodes.summary: Zhang et al. (2024) propose evaluating citation faithfulness metrics against three support levels: full, partial, and no support.

sources.title: Towards Fine-Grained Citation Evaluation in Generated Text: A Comparative Analysis of Faithfulness Metrics

nodes.label: No consistently best fine-grained citation faithfulness metric
nodes.summary: Zhang et al. (2024) report that no single citation-faithfulness metric consistently performs best across their fine-grained evaluations.

sources.title: Towards Fine-Grained Citation Evaluation in Generated Text: A Comparative Analysis of Faithfulness Metrics

nodes.label: Context-prior augmented citation evaluation dimensions
nodes.summary: Shen et al. (2025) introduce a citation-generation task considering external context and internal model knowledge, evaluated with five metrics addressing helpfulness, citation faithfulness, and trustworthiness.

sources.title: Transparentize the Internal and External Knowledge Utilization in LLMs with Trustworthy Citation

nodes.label: MIRAGE saliency-based answer attribution
nodes.summary: Qi et al. (2024) describe MIRAGE as identifying context-sensitive answer tokens and attributing them to retrieved documents using saliency methods.

sources.title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation

nodes.label: Fluent counterfactuals for attribution-faithfulness evaluation
nodes.summary: Kamahi et al. (2024) argue that removing or corrupting input tokens creates out-of-distribution inputs for autoregressive language models and propose fluent in-distribution counterfactuals for evaluating attribution methods.

sources.title: Counterfactuals As a Means for Evaluating Faithfulness of Attribution Methods in Autoregressive Language Models

nodes.label: CLAIM-BENCH observed scientific claim-evidence reasoning limitations
nodes.summary: Javaji et al. (2025) report substantial limitations in processing scientific claim-evidence relationships when evaluating six LLMs on more than 300 claim-evidence pairs across multiple research domains.

sources.title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim →Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers

nodes.label: Multi-pass prompting tradeoff in CLAIM-BENCH
nodes.summary: Javaji et al. (2025) report that three-pass and one-by-one prompting improve LLM claim-to-evidence linking in their evaluations, with increased computational cost.

sources.title: Can AI Validate Science? Benchmarking LLMs on Claim →Evidence Reasoning in AI Papers

nodes.label: FaithfulRAG models context-prior conflicts at fact level
nodes.summary: Zhang et al. (2025) propose FaithfulRAG, which identifies fact-level conflicts between retrieved context and model knowledge and uses a self-thinking process before generating responses.

sources.title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation

nodes.label: Reported Context-DPO context-faithfulness improvements
nodes.summary: Bi et al. (2025) report Context-DPO context-faithfulness improvements of 35% to 280% on popular open-source models in their experiments.

sources.title: Context-DPO: Aligning Language Models for Context-Faithfulness

nodes.label: High Plains well-derived groundwater depletion through 2007

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

nodes.label: GRACE-derived Central Valley groundwater depletion during 2006–2010
nodes.summary: Scanlon and colleagues report GRACE-derived Central Valley groundwater depletion of 6–8 km³ per year, totaling 24–34 km³, between April 2006 and March 2010.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

nodes.label: USGS High Plains recoverable groundwater storage through 2019
nodes.summary: McGuire and Strauch estimate that the High Plains aquifer contained approximately 2.91 billion acre-feet of recoverable groundwater in 2019, representing a decline of 286.4 million acre-feet, about 10%, since predevelopment.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

nodes.label: High Plains short-period groundwater recovery, 2017–2019
nodes.summary: McGuire and Strauch report a High Plains aquifer area-weighted average water-level rise of 0.1 foot and an estimated increase of 1.6 million acre-feet of recoverable groundwater storage during 2017–2019.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

nodes.label: High Plains specific-yield assumptions in recoverable storage estimates
nodes.summary: The USGS High Plains report gives an area-weighted mean specific yield of 15.1% for the aquifer excluding areas of little or no saturated thickness, with state means ranging from 8.1% in Wyoming to 18.5% in Oklahoma.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

sources.title: Estimating water levels in the High Plains Aquifer by synthesizing satellite data with groundwater well observations

nodes.summary: Choe and Ramdas report an adjust-then-combine procedure lifting e-processes across filtrations, with a logarithmic validity-recovery cost.

nodes.summary: Dwork et al. report that adaptive holdout reuse risks overfitting and propose an algorithm to validate many adaptively chosen hypotheses while avoiding that overfitting.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse

nodes.label: Lee et al. selection-conditional inference for lasso
nodes.summary: Lee et al. report selection-conditional inference for lasso-selected coefficients, including confidence intervals and tests.

sources.title: Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso

nodes.summary: The authors report experimental confirmation of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena formula in a trapped-ion implementation of the HaPPY holographic code.
